findings.description: The security group allows TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on a publicly addressable instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.

Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 serving cleartext HTTP, and egress is unrestricted to all destinations on all protocols, which permits data exfiltration and command-and-control traffic from a compromised host.

The user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in cleartext. EC2 user data is retrievable by anyone with instance access or SSRF against the metadata service, leaking long-lived IAM credentials.

No metadata_options block is specified, so IMDSv1 remains enabled on an internet-facing instance; combined with a public web server this creates an SSRF path to instance credentials and to the secrets stored in user data.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is configured, so the root EBS volume storing OS and application data is unencrypted at rest.

The instance is launched into a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and routed to an internet gateway, placing it directly on the public internet with no load balancer, bastion, or NAT boundary in front of it.
The EBS data volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so data written to the attached disk is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume and therefore inherits no encryption, leaving a second unencrypted copy of the data that can be shared or copied across accounts.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so network telemetry that reveals internal topology and traffic patterns is stored unencrypted.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or bucket policy restricts the flow log bucket, so a later ACL or policy change could expose sensitive network logs publicly. Defence in depth for the account's Block Public Access settings is absent.
The bucket has no policy denying non-HTTPS (aws:SecureTransport = false) requests, permitting flow log data to be read or written over cleartext HTTP.

findings.issue_category: Force destroy and no versioning on log store
findings.description: force_destroy = true with no versioning or object lock on an audit log destination allows security evidence to be deleted without trace, undermining log integrity.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true means every instance launched in this subnet receives a public IP and is reachable from the internet via the 0.0.0.0/0 internet gateway route, removing network segmentation by default.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true exposes all instances launched into this subnet directly to the internet through the shared default route to the internet gateway.

The VPC's default security group is not managed or restricted with aws_default_security_group, so resources attached to it inherit the default allow-all intra-group rules rather than an explicit deny-all baseline.
